title: Finite local charts for arbitrary pullbacks of sheafified representables
statement:
Let $\mathcal C$ be a small site [def-weil-pbc-sites-and-cohomology, def-weil-size-convention] with finite limits and a topology generated by a pretopology of finite covering families. Put $\mathcal E=\operatorname{Sh}(\mathcal C)$ and $H_U=h_U^\#$, where $h_U(T)=\operatorname{Hom}_{\mathcal C}(T,U)$ and $(-)^\#$ is sheafification [def-weil-pbc-sheafification]. Each $H_U$ is quasi-compact [def-trf-coherent-topos]. The family $(H_U)_{U\in\mathcal C}$ generates $\mathcal E$, and every quasi-compact object admits an epimorphism from a finite coproduct of its members. For every sheaf $F$ there is a natural bijection $\operatorname{Hom}(H_U,F)\simeq F(U)$. The functor $U\mapsto H_U$ preserves finite limits of diagrams in $\mathcal C$; in particular $H_1\simeq1$ and $H_V\times H_W\simeq H_{V\times W}$. For arbitrary morphisms $b:H_V\to H_U$ and $c:H_W\to H_U$ in $\mathcal E$, there exist finite covering families $(V_a\to V)_{a\in A}$ and $(W_d\to W)_{d\in D}$ and arrows $v_a:V_a\to U$, $w_d:W_d\to U$ such that $b|_{H_{V_a}}=H(v_a)$ and $c|_{H_{W_d}}=H(w_d)$. The canonical family
$$\bigl(H_{V_a\times_U W_d}\longrightarrow H_V\times_{H_U}H_W\bigr)_{(a,d)\in A\times D}$$
is jointly epimorphic, and $H_V\times_{H_U}H_W$ is quasi-compact [def-trf-coherent-topos]. The conclusion holds without assuming the topology subcanonical or either morphism globally induced by a site arrow.

proof.text: Let $K$ be the pretopology of the hypothesis: its members are finite covering families of the site, and the topology generated by the site's coverings is the topology $J_K$ generated by $K$. By [lem-weil-pbc-pretopology-sheaf-condition], applied to $K$ (its isomorphism, composition and pullback axioms hold, and all fibre products exist here), $J_K$ consists of the sieves on $U$ that contain the members of some family in $K$. A covering family $(U_i\to U)_{i\in I}$ generates a sieve $R\in J_K(U)$, so $R$ contains a finite family $(V_j\to U)_{j\in J}\in K$. Membership in $R$ means each $V_j\to U$ factors through some $U_{\alpha(j)}\to U$; choose these factorizations. As $J$ is finite, $\alpha$ has finite image, so condition (i) of [lem-trf-site-quasicompact-sheafification-criterion] holds for every $U$. Its implication (i)$\Rightarrow$(ii) proves that each $H_U$ is quasi-compact.

By the universal property in [def-weil-pbc-sheafification], restriction along $h_U\to H_U$ identifies $\operatorname{Hom}(H_U,F)$ with $\operatorname{Hom}(h_U,F)$. Compose with [lem-galois-yoneda-hom-bijection] to get the asserted bijection, explicitly $t\mapsto t_U(\eta_U(\mathrm{id}_U))$. Both bijections are natural, so precomposition by $H(f)$ corresponds to restriction along $f$, and postcomposition corresponds to applying a sheaf morphism. No full faithfulness of sheafified Yoneda is asserted.

For a sheaf $F$, take one map $H_T\to F$ for every pair $(T,s)$ with $s\in F(T)$, using step 2. The pairs form a set by smallness and the containing-universe convention. Each section $s$ lifts through its own component, using $\eta_T(\mathrm{id}_T)$. The local-lifting criterion in [lem-trf-topos-finite-cover-calculus](1), with the identity covering, says that this family is jointly epimorphic. Hence $(H_T)_T$ generates. If $F$ is quasi-compact, its definition in [def-trf-coherent-topos] selects a finite subfamily of these maps, giving the required finite coproduct epimorphism.

source.place: Tag 00WS (lemma-sheaf-coequalizer-representable), first paragraph of proof; Tag 0D07 (definition-quasi-compact-topos).

proof.text: For a finite diagram $D$ of site objects and its limit $L$, the defining universal property gives, naturally in $T$, $h_L(T)=\operatorname{Hom}(T,L)\simeq\lim_i\operatorname{Hom}(T,D_i)$. These are the presheaf-limit bijections: compatible maps into the presheaves $h_{D_i}$ factor uniquely objectwise through $h_L$, and uniqueness makes the factorization natural. Thus $h_L\simeq\lim_i h_{D_i}$. Apply finite-limit preservation in [lem-weil-pbc-sheafification-sets-exact] to obtain $H_L\simeq\lim_i H_{D_i}$, with the prescribed projection maps. This includes the empty diagram, products, and pullbacks of actual site arrows.

source.place: Tag 00WJ (lemma-sheafification-exact); representable limit calculation by the universal property.

proof.text: Under step 2 the arrow $b:H_V\to H_U$ corresponds to a section $\beta\in h_U^\#(V)$. Apply [lem-weil-pbc-site-sheafification-sections-local] with presheaf $h_U$ to obtain a covering $(V_i\to V)$ and arrows $v_i:V_i\to U$ representing $\beta$ locally. Refine this cover by a finite covering $(V_a\to V)$ as in step 1, and compose each representative with its refinement arrow. Naturality in step 2 identifies the resulting equality of sections with $b|_{H_{V_a}}=H(v_a)$. Apply exactly this construction to $c$ and its section of $h_U^\#(W)$ to obtain a finite cover $(W_d\to W)$ and arrows $w_d$ with the claimed restriction equality. Only local representation, not global representation or subcanonicity, has been used.

source.place: Tag 00WK (lemma-sections-sheafification), applied to $h_U$; finite refinement from step 1.

proof.text: The site covers $(V_a\to V)$ and $(W_d\to W)$ give jointly epimorphic sheaf families: apply [lem-trf-site-epimorphic-family-cover-lifts] with sections $\eta_{V_a}(\mathrm{id}_{V_a})$ and $\eta_{W_d}(\mathrm{id}_{W_d})$, respectively. The required lift equations are the naturality equations for the units. By [lem-trf-topos-finite-cover-calculus](1), the family $H_{V_a}\times_{H_U}H_{W_d}\to H_V\times_{H_U}H_W$ is jointly epimorphic. Its two structure maps to $H_U$ are $H(v_a)$ and $H(w_d)$ by step 5. Step 4 therefore identifies each domain, with its projections, with $H_{V_a\times_U W_d}$. These projection-compatible identifications give exactly the canonical family in the statement.

source.place: Tag 00WT (lemma-covering-surjective-after-sheafification), Tag 00W2 (lemma-limit-sheaf); finite-limit identification from step 4.

proof.text: The set $A\times D$ is finite, and every $V_a\times_U W_d$ is a site object by finite limits. Step 1 makes all $H_{V_a\times_U W_d}$ quasi-compact. Apply [lem-trf-topos-finite-cover-calculus](3) to the finite jointly epimorphic family of step 6: its target $H_V\times_{H_U}H_W$ is quasi-compact. This also covers empty $A$ or $D$, since that statement includes the empty finite coproduct and its epimorphic images.
